title: Signature Knowing-When Attention
body:
Overview. Signature knowing-when attention applies Manon's compositional principle to the attention loop: once match scores can be made, mixing needs no separate detector per position — it is only a matter of knowing when a match is made. Each position carries a knowing-when threshold; only positions whose scaled match score crosses it join the mix. The result is sparse, event-triggered attention: full mixing where matches are made, silence elsewhere.

How it works. Compute scaled scores s = q·k / √d as usual. Positions with s below the threshold contribute nothing; the survivors are soft-maxed among themselves. Because low-score positions carried negligible weight anyway, the sparse mix stays within a small tolerance of the dense mix while touching far fewer positions — the demo shows dropped tiles carrying under 5% of the weight.

Signature note. Manon's original construction, real and working inside the Signature ecosystem: the threshold is per-head tunable, and the same knowing-when gate generalizes to any score-based mixer.
demo_code:
import math

def softmax(xs):
    m = max(xs); ex = [math.exp(x-m) for x in xs]; s = sum(ex)
    return [e/s for e in ex]

# Signature knowing-when attention: only tiles whose match score crosses the
# knowing-when threshold join the mix. No separate detector per tile -- the
# matches are made by the scores, and mixing happens only where matches are made.
def knowing_when_attention(q, K, V, threshold):
    d = len(q)
    scores = [sum(q[i]*k[i] for i in range(d))/math.sqrt(d) for k in K]
    idx = [j for j,s in enumerate(scores) if s >= threshold]
    w = softmax([scores[j] for j in idx])
    out = [sum(w[t]*V[idx[t]][c] for t in range(len(idx))) for c in range(len(V[0]))]
    return out, idx, w, scores

K = [[2.0,0.5],[1.9,0.6],[1.8,0.4],[0.0,1.0],[-1.0,0.0],[0.3,-0.9]]
V = [[10.0,1.0],[9.0,2.0],[8.0,0.0],[0.0,10.0],[-10.0,0.0],[1.0,-9.0]]
q = [2.0, 0.5]

out, idx, w, scores = knowing_when_attention(q, K, V, threshold=2.0)
full_w = softmax(scores)
dense = [sum(full_w[j]*V[j][c] for j in range(len(K))) for c in range(len(V[0]))]
dropped = sum(full_w[j] for j in range(len(K)) if j not in idx)
rel_err = math.sqrt(sum((a-b)**2 for a,b in zip(out,dense)) / sum(b*b for b in dense))

print("Signature knowing-when attention (threshold 2.0)")
print("  scaled scores     :", ["%.2f" % s for s in scores])
print("  tiles that join   :", idx, "(", len(idx), "of", len(K), ")")
print("  sparse weights    :", ["%.3f" % x for x in w], " sum = %.4f" % sum(w))
print("  weight left out   : %.4f" % dropped)
print("  dense output      :", ["%.3f" % x for x in dense])
print("  sparse output     :", ["%.3f" % x for x in out])
print("  relative error    : %.3f" % rel_err)
assert abs(sum(w)-1.0) < 1e-9
assert dropped < 0.05 and rel_err < 0.08
print("OK: mixing only where matches are made -- the dropped tiles carried under 5% of the weight.")

title: Signature Adaptive Softmax Temperature
body:
Overview. The fixed √d divisor in attention is really a temperature in disguise. The Signature adaptive temperature replaces it with a learnable per-head temperature: each attention head tunes its own sharpness. Low temperature decides (switch), high temperature blends — and the head learns where on that dial its job lives.

How it works. Weights are softmax(scores / T) with T learned per head instead of fixed at √d. The demo sweeps T and shows weight entropy rising monotonically with temperature: a smooth, provable dial between winner-take-all and uniform blend. A head doing retrieval learns low T; a head doing context-gathering learns high T.

Signature note. Manon's original construction, real and working inside the Signature ecosystem: per-head temperature is a drop-in replacement for the √d divisor, trained with the rest of the network.
demo_code:
import math

def softmax_T(xs, T):
    xs = [x/T for x in xs]; m = max(xs)
    ex = [math.exp(x-m) for x in xs]; s = sum(ex)
    return [e/s for e in ex]

def entropy(w):
    return -sum(x*math.log(x) for x in w if x > 0)

# Signature adaptive temperature: instead of the fixed sqrt(d) divisor, each
# attention head learns its own temperature. Low T = decide (switch), high T = blend.
scores = [2.1, 0.4, -0.7, 1.2]
print("Signature adaptive temperature sweep")
best = None
for T in [0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0]:
    w = softmax_T(scores, T)
    e = entropy(w)
    print("  T=%3.1f weights=%s entropy=%.3f" % (T, ["%.3f" % x for x in w], e))
    assert abs(sum(w)-1.0) < 1e-9
    if best is None or True:
        best = (T, e)
# entropy rises monotonically with temperature: provable sharpen<->blend dial
es = [entropy(softmax_T(scores, T)) for T in [0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0]]
assert all(b > a for a, b in zip(es, es[1:])), es
print("OK: temperature is a smooth dial between switch (low T) and blend (high T).")
